# CVE-2026-58192 — Appium storage-plugin: unauthenticated arbitrary file/directory deletion via the delete endpoint

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

| **CVE** | CVE-2026-58192 |
| **Component** | `@appium/storage-plugin` — `deleteStorageItem` handler (`plugin.js`), `Storage.delete` (`storage.js`) |
| **Affected** | < 1.1.6 |
| **Fixed in** | **1.1.6** — GHSA-jwgx-mp9m-jwcr |
| **CWE** | CWE-22 (Path Traversal) |
| **Impact** | An unauthenticated remote client sends `POST /storage/delete` with a `name` containing `../`; the handler deletes it from the storage folder without sanitization, escaping the storage root and recursively deleting arbitrary files/directories the Appium process user can write |
| **Vector** | Network — unauthenticated HTTP endpoint |
| **Trigger** | `POST /storage/delete` body `{"name": "../victim"}` |

The vulnerable delete handler passed the name straight through to the
recursive delete:

```js
// @appium/storage-plugin 1.1.5, deleteStorageItem
STORAGE_HANDLERS.deleteStorageItem = async function (req) {
    return await executeStorageMethod(async (storage) =>
        await storage.delete(parseRequestArgs(req, ['name']).name));  // no validation
};
// Storage.delete: path.join(this._root, name) -> fs.rimraf(destinationPath)
```

The fix validates the name first (matching the upload path):

```js
// 1.1.6, deleteStorageItem
name = parseRequestArgs(req, ['name']).name;
validateStorageItemName(name);   // rejects traversal / special-character names
return await executeStorageMethod(async (storage) => await storage.delete(name));
```

with no path sanitization or containment check. `path.join` does not collapse
